'''David Norman''' (born 1949) is a British [[Chartered Physicist]]<ref name="EN-acting">{{cite web|url=http://www.english-nature.org.uk/news/story.asp?ID=200 |title=English Nature announce acting Chairman |date=2000-09-28 |publisher=English Nature |access-date=2008-11-26 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070722103722/http://www.english-nature.org.uk/news/story.asp?ID=200 |archivedate=2007-07-22 }}</ref> and [[ornithology|ornithologist]], he has lived in [[Cheshire]] since 1978.<ref name="RBBP-pan">{{cite web|url=http://www.rbbp.org.uk/rbbp-panel.htm|title=Current Panel Members|publisher=Rare Breeding Birds Panel|access-date=2008-11-27|archive-date=31 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231063657/http://rbbp.org.uk/rbbp-panel.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Physics==

Professor Norman is a former director of synchrotron radiation, [[Council for the Central Laboratory of the Research Councils]], [[Daresbury Laboratory]].<ref name="EN-acting" /> He was a visiting professor in surface science at the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref name="EN-acting" />

== Ornithology ==

Since 2005<ref name="BB100:6">{{cite journal|last=Holling|first=Mark|author2=The Rare Breeding Birds Panel|date=June 2007|title=Rare breeding birds in the United Kingdom in 2003 and 2004|url=http://www.rbbp.org.uk/downloads/rbbp-report-2003-04.pdf|journal=British Birds|volume=100|issue=6|pages=321–367|issn=0007-0335|access-date=29 August 2015|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924084945/http://www.rbbp.org.uk/downloads/rbbp-report-2003-04.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>, he has been an independent member of the United Kingdom's [[Rare Breeding Birds Panel]]<ref name="RSPB-council">{{cite web|url=http://www.rspb.org.uk/about/run/council.asp |title=RSPB Council |publisher=RSPB |access-date=2008-11-26 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080303044502/http://www.rspb.org.uk/about/run/council.asp |archivedate=2008-03-03 }}</ref> and he is a member of the [[RSPB]] Council,<ref name="RSPB-council" /> and chairman of the Merseyside Ringing Group. He is an honorary research associate of the [[Carnegie Museum of Natural History]],<ref name="RSPB-council" /> spending up to a month each year at their [[Powdermill Nature Reserve]].<ref name="RBBP-pan" />

He served on the council of [[English Nature]] from 1996 to 2002 (and in September 2000 became interim acting chairman for six months).<ref name="EN-acting" /><ref name="RBBP-pan" /> He has been chairman of the [[Cheshire Wildlife Trust]]<ref name="RBBP-pan" /> and a member of the Editorial Board for Ornithology's journal ''Ringing & Migration''.<ref name="EN-acting" /> He was the founder chairman of the Mersey Estuary Conservation Group<ref name="EN-acting" /> and Research Committee of the Liverpool Bay Wader Study Group.<ref name="EN-acting" />

In 2002, he was awarded the [[British Trust for Ornithology]]'s [[Bernard Tucker Medal]] "for his outstanding scientific contributions in surveying, nest-recording and ringing birds".<ref name="BTO-med">{{cite web|url=http://www.bto.org/aboutBTO/accounts/medallists.htm|title=Medallists|date=2006-06-02|publisher=BTO|access-date=2008-11-27}}</ref>
